edges.effect_quant: Prospective cohort data suggest the direction is more reliable than any single pooled magnitude.
edges.population: offspring of mothers with higher pregnancy UPF intake
edges.mechanism: This early-life or prenatal exposure may shape Childhood obesity through developmental programming, microbiome establishment, immune maturation, or nutrient sufficiency during sensitive windows. Timing matters because the same exposure can be much more consequential in infancy or pregnancy than later in life.
edges.summary: Maternal diet high in ultra-processed food appears tied to higher risk of childhood obesity in offspring of mothers with higher pregnancy UPF intake mainly through prospective cohort data. The likely magnitude is modest, which is why the edge is framed conservatively rather than as a headline-level breakthrough.
edges.caveats: Dose, timing, and baseline risk still matter. Observational edges may partly reflect broader lifestyle patterning, while small trials can overstate benefit if follow-up is short.
